raw_response:
I farm only 3.5 mu, so I count every bag, but I still will not save money by cutting fertilizer too much. On my land in Quzhou, I do what has worked these years: wheat first, then maize after wheat. I have well irrigation, so I can push yield more steadily than depending only on rain. I finished middle school, so I do look at cost and also at what gives a stable harvest. I will mostly follow what I used last year, then adjust a little by watching nearby fields. For wheat, I will use a good improved variety, put enough base fertilizer in, water it about three times if the season is normal, and spray twice so rust, aphids, and later disease do not get ahead of me. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, because around here hybrids pay better if the stand is good. I will keep fertilizer a bit stronger on maize, because if maize runs short at the big growth stage, yield drops fast and I cannot get it back later. Since my farm is small and family labor is limited because some people work outside, I will keep tillage simple with rotary work and avoid anything too complicated. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer and hold yield than save a little money and regret it at harvest.
